description.narrative:
Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work (FPRW), with special focus on combating child labour, were mainstreamed in the Labour and Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) national inspection checklist to better identify, report and advice on working conditions with special new feature enabling referring child labour cases. The updated OSH inspection checklist was required to better respond to biological hazards and labour inspection checklists were updated to include the newly adopted laws for people with disabilities and women night work related ministerial decrees. The inspection checklists were validated by national inspectors and adopted by the Ministry of Manpower. Accordingly, Labour and OSH inspectors were capacitated on the newly adopted checklists.
The ILO Dutch Funded ACCEL Africa Project in Egypt provided technical assistants to the Ministry of Manpower to updating the national inspection checklists and conducting consultation and validation sessions with national OSH and Labour Inspectors to enhance the checklists before being adopted by the Ministry in January 2021.
ACCEL Africa Project developed and implemented Capacity building Programme targeting 350 national OSH and Labour inspectors capacitated on the newly adopted inspection checklists by September 2021. In collaboration with the Ministry of Manpower, the ILO has introduced an innovative awareness service (tele-advisory services) that targets national OSH field inspectors across Egypt during COVID-19 Pandemic, targeting 569 MOM OSH field inspectors that were capacitated on the newly adopted checklists by September 2021.

description.narrative:
In March 2020, the tripartite constituents launched an integrated programme to support the implementation of the new trade union law, strengthen inclusive social dialogue and improve compliance with FPRW in the apparel sector.
Within the framework of this programme, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for the process of registering trade unions, as well as an analysis of the High Council for Social Dialogue were finalized. One of the key objectives of the SOP is to make the trade union registration process more transparent and accessible to workers organisations As a direct result, 47 trade union committees have been registered and have received legal identity.
A protocol was put in place concerning serious rights violations – including on FPRW. The protocol defines the process to report such violations and remediate them.
As a result of compliance assessments 50 factories in the apparel sector have improved their benchmark performance on FPRW, in accordance with the principles of the related ILO conventions. With support of the ILO and Better Work revenue, technical assistance has been provided to the Government and social partners to enhance mechanisms for inclusive social dialogue and operationalize the new trade union law.
Through the Better Work programme, 50 enrolled factories underwent a detailed and unannounced compliance assessment including on FPWR. Based on the results from the compliance assessments, tailored training and advisory services were offered to the companies to enhance their knowledge of the ILO conventions on FPRW and subsequently improve compliance levels with regards to child labour, forced labour, non-discrimination and freedom of association and collective bargaining.
The Better Work programme also engaged with over 20 international buyers and retailers sourcing from these companies in Egypt in order to build sustainability of compliance improvement efforts at the enterprise level.

description.narrative: • In late 2020, a Trade Union (TU) Grievance Committee was established and institutionalized by a Ministerial Decree No. 162/2020. The purpose of the committee is to conduct dialogue between the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and pending TUs and to provide a sustainable technical support for TUs and workers trying to establish/ register a TU. The committee is also set to work with other MOM's directorates throughout the country to ensure consistency in the application of procedures and standards. Consequently, a list of 78 TUs under registration was prepared to be discussed through the committee. Since 9 November 2020, 42 cases were discussed in 14 hearings with ILO staff presence as observers, resulting in the successful registration of 28 TUs. The TU Grievance Committee supported the registration of 27 other TU Committees through individual meeting to reach the total of 55 TU registered committees. •Standing Operating Procedures (SOPs) were developed in a consultative manner accordingly to map, unify and simplify TU registration process and make it transparent to all constituents. The SOPs is currently reviewed by MOM to be validated. It is expected to be issued in September 2021. • A Prime Ministerial Decree concerning the formation of the High Council for Social Dialogue is expected to be issued before the end of the year. As a result of the ILO RBSA TA project (EGY 20/1/RBS) Strengthen Labour Relations and Their Institutions in Egypt" (SLARIE), four rounds of inclusive virtual and physical consultations with the tripartite were conducted to discuss the difficulties of TU registration process and social dialogue institutionalizations and improvement. • The ILO also conveyed 4 tripartite inclusive meetings bringing together all relevant representatives of the tripartite constituents with leaving no one behind where they considerably discussed the application difficulties of the newly amended trade union laws. As a result of this inclusive dialogue, the tripartite constituents came up with a set of recommendations and actions to resolve those difficulties including establishing a Trade Union Grievance Committee to discuss and resolve pending TU's cases and developing Standing Operating Procedures (SOPs) to unify and simplify TU registration process that was drafted in a consultative manner accordingly to map, unify and simplify TU registration process and make it transparent to all constituents. • The project has provided technical support and facilitation to the meetings conducted by the Trade Union (TU) Grievance Committee that has resulted in 14 hearings since November 9, 2020 at MOM's premises. • The ILO reviewed the draft HCSD decree and proposed areas for improvement pertaining to its name, mandate, operationalization and tripartite representation. This work was done in close consultation with employers' and workers representatives. The Ministry of Manpower subsequently approved the proposal, with some minor comments and passed it to the PM's office.
